item.title: Formal Neighborhood Equivariant Cohomology and Kirwan Surjectivity at Singular Values
item.description: arXiv:2610.35936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(G\) be a compact Lie group acting Hamiltonianly on a symplectic manifold \(M\) with moment map \(\mu:M\to\g^*\). For a singular value \(a\) of \(\mu\), the symplectic quotient \(\mu^{-1}(a)/G\) is stratified and the classical Kirwan map is not defined. We introduce a \emph{formal neighborhood equivariant cohomology} \(\cH_G^*(a)\) using the slice-groupoid Cartan sheaf and the closed embedding \(\mu^{-1}(a)/G\hookrightarrow \mu^{-1}(U_a)/G\) for a \(G\)-invariant neighborhood \(U_a\) of \(a\). We define a formal Kirwan map \[ \kappa_{\mathrm{formal}}:H_G^*(M)\longrightarrow \cH_G^*(a). \] We prove that \(\kappa_{\mathrm{formal}}\) is surjective under a local \emph{equivariant homotopy retraction} condition on the slice level sets \[ C_x=\mu_x^{-1}(a|_{\g_x})\subset S_x, \] which is satisfied, for example, when \(a\) is a regular value of every slice moment map, or when \(a=0\) and \(C_x\) is a \(G_x\)-equivariant cone. The weakest condition we identify is the existence, for each \(x\in\mu^{-1}(a)\), of a local quasi-isomorphism \[ \Car(S_x,G_x)\simeq \cC^\bullet_{C_x} \] in a \(G_x\)-equivariant neighborhood of the orbit, without requiring a global tubular neighborhood. As an application we recover, in the formal framework, the even-degree surjectivity theorem of Delarue--Ramacher--Schmitt for \(S^1\)-actions and clarify why odd-degree surjectivity fails in general.
item.dc:creator: Zhenxi Huang

item.title: Rigidity and Affine Deformations of Foliations on Nilpotent and Solvable Contact Lie Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.35940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let g be a Lie algebra of dimension 2n+1, let beta be a contact form, and let alpha be a nonzero integrable 1-form. We study when the affine path alpha_t = (1-t)alpha + t beta consists of contact forms with the orientation determined by beta \wedge (d beta)^n. We first establish an algebraic criterion: affine deformability is equivalent to the non-negativity of a scalar obtained from the interaction form Theta(alpha, beta) = alpha \wedge (d beta)^n + n beta \wedge d alpha \wedge (d beta)^{n-1}. For unimodular Lie algebras this scalar is (n+1)alpha(Z_beta), where Z_beta is the Reeb vector. We also derive a formula involving the modular character tau(X) = tr(ad_X) in the non-unimodular case. On nilpotent contact Lie algebras, every integrable 1-form is closed; using the standard structural properties of nilpotent contact Lie algebras, this implies that every left-invariant foliation is an affine origin for every fixed contact form. An explicit three-dimensional example illustrates that the modular term can yield affine deformability even when alpha(Z_beta) = 0. We discuss the implications for left-invariant forms on Lie groups and compact quotients. We do not claim a general obstruction example in the non-unimodular case; establishing such an example requires a separate verified construction.
item.dc:creator: Cheikh Khoule, Rafik Khalfi

item.title: Spectral $\Gamma_2$ inequalities for the $V$-Laplacian with evolving weighted measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.36091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish spectral Bakry-\'{E}mery $\Gamma_2$ criteria and their modified counterparts for the $V$-Laplacian on closed Riemannian manifolds equipped with evolving weighted measures. The estimates yield jointly optimized spectral bounds and sharp endpoint constants. When the measures evolve according to the Fokker-Planck equation, these estimates yield monotonicity formulas for the Fisher information associated with Shannon and Tsallis entropies, together with quantitative propagation of Poincar\'e, logarithmic Sobolev, and nonlinear interpolation inequalities. In the stationary reversible setting, our results specialize to the Witten Laplacian and recover the unweighted Cai-Wang estimates \cite{Cai}.
item.dc:creator: Ha Tuan Dung, Yi Li

item.title: $L^p$ Convergence of AMV Laplacians on completions of Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.36125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study conditions for the $L^p$ convergence of the AMV Laplacian $\Delta_r$ on completions of Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$. The condition invloves the Minkowski dimension of the set $\overline{M} \setminus M$ and how much the curvature is blowing up around $S$. We build a concrete family of sets that satisfies these conditions, and provide an example of non convergence when these conditions are not met.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Dias

item.title: A convexity theorem for proper Dupin hypersurfaces in spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.36366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that if $M$ is a (compact, connected, and embedded) proper Dupin hypersurface in a sphere then, viewing $M$ as a submanifold of the ambient Euclidean space, its orthogonal projection to the normal space at any point is convex. This is a generalization of the convexity theorem of Terng for isoparametric submanifolds in Euclidean spaces.
item.dc:creator: Augustin-Liviu Mare

item.title: $O(3)$-symmetry of four-dimensional steady Ricci solitons
item.description: arXiv:2610.36563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a complete connected four-dimensional gradient steady Ricci soliton with positive curvature operator that is $\kappa$-noncollapsed at all scales admits an effective isometric $O(3)$ action preserving the potential function and having principal orbits diffeomorphic to $S^2$.
item.dc:creator: Hanbing Fang

item.title: Grassmannian Realizations of Classical Pseudo-Riemannian Symmetric Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.36724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a unified fixed-point Grassmannian framework for the classical pseudo-Riemannian symmetric spaces from Berger's classification. For a classical group $G=\mathop{\mathrm{Aut}}(V,b)$, we identify $G$ with the open graph-like locus inside an ordinary or maximal-isotropic Grassmannian $\overline{G}$. Natural involutions of $\overline{G}$ are constructed via classical forms, compatible scalar structures, and subspace configurations. We explicitly describe the full fixed loci of these involutions in terms of classical Grassmannians. The corresponding graph-like fixed loci (or their signature strata) are identified, respectively, with the moduli spaces of classical forms, compatible scalar structures, and subspace configurations; these moduli spaces coincide with classical pseudo-Riemannian symmetric spaces. In summary, the 54 classical series are organized into four families: 10 group-type models, 7 classical-form Grassmannians, 20 scalar-structure Grassmannians, and 17 subspace-configuration Grassmannians.
item.dc:creator: Yunxia Chen, Naichung Conan Leung

item.title: The Costa surface with a free-boundary hole: an embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with three ends
item.description: arXiv:2610.36741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface outside the unit ball whose compact boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. By Mazet and Mendes, in $\mathbb{R}^3$ every such surface with one regular end is a catenoidal piece, and every stable one with parallel embedded regular ends is catenoidal. We construct connected embedded examples with three ends from the Costa surface $M$, placed so that its central saddle point is at the origin. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ we perturb $\varepsilon^{-1}(M\setminus B_\varepsilon)$ into a properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface of genus one with one boundary circle and three ends, two catenoidal and one planar. The construction is a small-hole perturbation. The only error of the initial surface is in the boundary condition. The symmetry group of the Costa surface removes all obstructions: at the hole it forbids the logarithmic and the tilting modes, and globally it kills the bounded Jacobi fields of the Costa surface, which is nondegenerate by Nayatani. In the conformal compactification the Jacobi operator is smooth also at the ends, so the linear analysis takes place on a compact torus with one small hole. The same construction applied to the Costa-Hoffman-Meeks surfaces gives such examples of every genus $k\geq1$, of index at least $2k+3$. We also report numerical experiments with two independent implementations of the Costa surface. They confirm the period condition, the symmetries, the boundary error, the index and nullity of the Jacobi operator and the absence of an equivariant kernel. They also compute the free-boundary correction near the hole, which gives pictures of the surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Igor Kozyrev

item.title: Cartan-Ambrose-Hicks theorems and dual geodesic symmetries on statistical manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.36803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish Cartan-Ambrose-Hicks (CAH) theorems for statistical manifolds and characterize statistical symmetric spaces by dual geodesic symmetries. These theorems determine statistical structures up to local statisticmorphism by comparing the curvature of an alpha-connection and the skewness tensor using radial geodesics and parallel displacement of that connection. The Levi-Civita formulation characterizes local statisticmorphisms by comparing the radial Jacobi operators of Riemannian curvature and the skewness tensor using Levi-Civita parallel displacement. The same characterization holds with statistical curvature in place of Riemannian curvature. For Hessian manifolds, comparison of the skewness tensor alone is necessary and sufficient. For connected statistical manifolds, we prove the equivalence between the homogeneous definition of statistical symmetric spaces and the existence of global dual geodesic symmetries at every point. The CAH theorems give the necessary and sufficient conditions for maps constructed from exponential maps of dual connections to be local dual geodesic symmetries, preserving the metric and interchanging the dual connections. Such local symmetries exist at every point if and only if the Riemannian curvature and skewness tensors are Levi-Civita parallel. For Hessian manifolds, this condition is equivalent to the equality of the Hessian and dual Hessian curvature tensors.
item.dc:creator: Naoto Satoh

item.title: Pontrjagin Classes of Locally Spherically Symmetric Projectively Affine Sprays
item.description: arXiv:2610.36841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By Chern--Weil theory, rational Pontrjagin classes are represented by curvature forms. Sprays, which require no metric and include all Finsler and Riemannian geodesic sprays, provide a natural setting for the vanishing problem. Shen and Zhao proved that if a manifold admits a locally projectively flat spray, then all of its rational Pontrjagin classes vanish. We ask whether this rigidity persists for the wider class of projectively affine sprays. We prove that if a smooth manifold admits a locally spherically symmetric projectively affine spray, then all rational Pontrjagin classes vanish. Stronger, the Pontrjagin forms of the associated Berwald spray vanish identically as differential forms, a genuine geometric rigidity. Hence a manifold with nonzero rational Pontrjagin class cannot carry such a spray; in particular, it admits no Riemannian metric whose geodesic spray is locally spherically symmetric. We also construct non-Berwald, non-projectively-flat examples with identically vanishing Pontrjagin forms, showing the phenomenon is not a byproduct of projective flatness.
item.dc:creator: Zuhuan Jia, Benling Li

item.title: Quantitative Rigidity of Ricci Nonnegative Manifolds via the Regular Green Constant
item.description: arXiv:2610.36998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a Ricci non-negative non-parabolic manifold $(M^{n\ge3},g)$, assuming the minimal normalized Green function admits the asymptotic expansion $G=r^{2-n}+H_p+O_1(r)$, we prove the scaling invariant defect $H_pR^{n-2}$ controls the geometry of the geodesic ball quantitatively, $\frac{1}{R}d_{GH}(B_p(R),B_0^{\mathbb{R}^n}(R))\le C_n \left(H_p R^{n-2}\right)^{\frac{1}{88(n+1)(4n+1)}}$.
item.dc:creator: Zhelei Huang, Bijia Luo, Jie Zhou

item.title: New inhomogeneous Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds with large symmetry group
item.description: arXiv:2610.37102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study compact non-K\"ahler Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds whose connected full group of holomorphic isometries acts with cohomogeneity one. We prove that the Lie algebra of this group is isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$ or $\mathbb{R}^2\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$, unless the Bismut connection is flat. We then focus on the first case, where we determine the possible singular isotropy algebras and reduce the Bismut Hermitian-Einstein condition to a system of ordinary differential equations. We obtain explicit solutions satisfying suitable smoothness conditions, that yield families of compact and complete non-compact non-K\"ahler Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds with non-constant scalar curvature and non-zero Bismut curvature, including examples on $S^3\times S^3$ and $S^3\times S^1\times\mathbb{R}^2$, respectively. We also investigate the topology of the compact examples and determine the asymptotic scalar curvature of the non-compact ones. Moreover, we prove the existence of a smooth deformation of a Bismut-flat Samelson structure on $S^3\times S^3$ through non-K\"ahler Bismut Hermitian-Einstein structures that are not Bismut-flat. The regularity of the constructed compact examples is also investigated.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Podest\`a, Alberto Raffero

item.title: Rigidity of Constant-Scalar-Curvature Ricci Shrinkers with Totally Geodesic Focal Set
item.description: arXiv:2610.37151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M^n,g,f)$ be a complete connected shrinking gradient Ricci soliton with constant scalar curvature, satisfying \[ \Ric+\nabla^2f=\frac12g. \] We prove that if the focal set of $f$ is totally geodesic, then $M$ is rigid. Equivalently, its universal cover is a product of a compact Einstein manifold and a Euclidean space.
item.dc:creator: Fengjiang Li, Wenqi Li, Jianyu Ou, Yuanyuan Qu, Guoqiang Wu, Detang Zhou

item.title: An Anisotropic Entropy for the Rotationally Symmetric Ricci Flow
item.dc:creator: Hongxin Guo, Guozhi Lin

item.title: On Landsberg Unicorns of General $(\alpha,\beta)$-Type
item.description: arXiv:2610.37241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the classes of \lq\lq unicorns" of general $(\alpha,\beta)$-metric types, namely, Landsberg general $(\alpha,\beta)$-metrics that are non-Berwaldian. We provide explicit solutions for these metrics, including several new classes. Furthermore, we identify and exclude the cases that yield degenerate metrics to guarantee the geometric validity of the established solutions.
item.dc:creator: Salah G. Elgendi

item.title: Localization of weighted Goldman volume on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\R)$-Hitchin Component
item.description: arXiv:2610.37317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute Goldman volume on the moduli space of convex real projective structures on a closed oriented surface of genus at least two, with exponential weight defined by the shifted Blaschke area. For every positive parameter, the integral converges and is a finite sum of inverse powers of that parameter. Its coefficients are intersection numbers involving the bundle of regular cubic differentials on the moduli stack of stable curves. The proof establishes absolute convergence and vanishing signed boundary integrals of the transgression under simultaneous plumbing degeneration. The pushforward of Goldman measure by the shifted Blaschke area therefore has a polynomial density on $[0,\infty)$, and its sublevel volumes are polynomial in the threshold.
item.dc:creator: Shiyu Cao

item.title: The Geometry of Manifold Learning: Singular foliations via Deep Learning models
item.description: arXiv:2610.37370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep learning algorithms have become widely used and successful across a wide range of tasks. A key challenge is determining whether these algorithms truly capture the intrinsic geometry of their training data in order to better understand what they learn from data. In this theoretical work, we explore a new geometric structure defined on the data space by a trained neural network through the Data Information Matrix (DIM), a variation of the Fisher Information Matrix. This new geometric structure is a foliation and the main focus of this work is to explore the non-smooth case of ReLU activation functions, where traditional geometric tools often fail. The foliation is defined through a distribution spanned by the columns of the DIM. We first prove that this distribution is non-smooth in the sense of distributions, rendering the existence of an associated foliation much more complex. To circumvent this issue, we introduce a smoothed version of this distribution that differs from the original only on a set of measure zero. Finally, we prove that this smoothed distribution induces a singular foliation on the data space, which is based on the data the network has been trained with. Our theoretical contributions provide a geometric framework to better understand how neural networks organize their input space in non-smooth settings, bridging differential geometry and deep learning theory.
item.dc:creator: Gabriele Novelli, Eliot Tron, Emanuele Latini, Rita Fioresi

item.title: A periodic minimal hypersurface in Euclidean 4-space with Clifford cone singularities
item.description: arXiv:2610.37453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\sigma(t)=\operatorname{sl}(\varpi t)$ be the lemniscatic sine, normalized to have period $2$. We study the zero set $\mathscr{M}$ of $S(x)=\sigma(x_1)\sigma(x_3)-\sigma(x_2)\sigma(x_4)$ in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$. We show that $\mathscr{M}$ is a complete embedded minimal hypersurface with infinitely many isolated singularities, which are exactly the vertices of the regular honeycomb of $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ by $24$-cells. Near every singular point $\mathscr{M}$ is an analytic image of the Clifford cone, and $\mathscr{M}$ is a stationary integral varifold with density $\pi/2$ at each singularity. The isometry group of $\mathscr{M}$ is generated by the translations of the root lattice $D_4$ and a hyperoctahedral group of order $384$ fixing the centre of a $24$-cell; it has index three in the symmetry group of the honeycomb, acts transitively on the singular points, and contains a symmetry which is not visible from the defining equation. Seen from the centre of a $24$-cell, $\mathscr{M}$ is the zero set of a theta series of a translate of the Hurwitz quaternions, which makes the whole symmetry group manifest; the sections of $\mathscr{M}$ by a family of parallel hyperplanes are triply periodic surfaces with cubic symmetry which change topology through conical points. Finally, $\mathscr{M}$ is obtained from a union of $2$-planes by attaching cones over $2$-tori, and its quotient by the lattice of periods is a compact minimal hypersurface in a flat $4$-torus with exactly three singular points and infinite Morse index; we show that its regular part is one-sided and compute its Euler characteristic and integral homology.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir G. Tkachev

item.title: Statistical Uniformization of Surfaces by Heat-Kernel Fisher Information
item.description: arXiv:2610.37520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Brownian particle observed at time $t$ carries information about where it started. On a closed surface this makes the surface itself a statistical model, whose Fisher information pulls back to a heat-smoothed metric $h_t=2tJ_t$; its volume $V_t$ is a normalized Jeffreys volume, and $\log(V_t/2t)$ is the model-dependent constant in Rissanen's minimum-description-length complexity. We ask whether maximizing this statistical size among metrics of fixed area in a conformal class recovers the uniformizing metric. First, $9(A-2\pi\chi t-V_t)/t^2$ converges to the curvature energy $\int K^2\,dA$ (the Calabi energy up to a topological constant), uniformly on classes of bounded geometry; hence, within a fixed-area conformal class of bounded geometry containing the uniformizer, approximate maximizers of $V_t$ converge to the constant-curvature metric (on the sphere, to the round metrics). Second, near every flat torus we prove a sharp finite-scale version: for small perturbations whose oscillations are resolved by the diffusion, $t|k|^2\le\theta<\tau_*$, the flat-subtracted defect is comparable to $\|\Delta f\|_2^2$, uniformly in the frequency cutoff and over noncollapsing lattices. The explicit threshold $\tau_*=4.408\ldots$ is optimal, and it is exactly the observation time at which the information about one curvature mode is maximal. Third, the flat structure is seen only at an exponential scale: the volume loss of a flat torus measures the ambiguity of winding and is comparable to $t^{-1/2}e^{-\operatorname{sys}^2/(16t)}$, which selects the hexagonal lattice as $t\to0$ but not at all times.
item.dc:creator: Gunhee Cho, Hyun Chul Jang

item.title: Contact topology and intrinsic characterization of transversely vanishing curl eigenforms
item.description: arXiv:2610.36212v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the geometry and topology of transversely vanishing eigenforms of the curl operator on $3$-manifolds, placing them in the broader framework of near-contact forms. We prove a Gray-type stability theorem for the kernels of near-contact forms, which we call near-contact structures, and derive a local neighborhood theorem around their singularities. As applications, we obtain a stability result for the contact topology of curl eigenforms, a classification of near-contact structures in terms of formal homotopical data, and a proof of the existence of contact structures on closed orientable 3-manifolds based on the spectral theory of the curl operator. We also study the symplectization of curl eigenforms as a possible bridge to symplectic dynamics. Finally, we characterize those transversely vanishing $1$-forms which are curl eigenforms for some smooth Riemannian metric. We deduce a generalization of the classical correspondence, due to Etnyre and Ghrist, between Reeb-like fields of contact forms and nowhere-vanishing rotational Beltrami fields to the setting of transversely vanishing vector fields.
item.dc:creator: Robert Cardona, Willi Kepplinger

item.title: Variations of the harmonic entropy and linear drift on negatively curved surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.36354v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For closed negatively curved surfaces, we obtain formulas for the derivatives of the harmonic entropy of its geodesic flow and the linear drift of its Brownian motion along conformal deformations. We deduce that the harmonic entropy of the geodesic flow of a closed surface of non-constant negative curvature (resp. linear drift of the Brownian motion on its universal cover) is strictly decreasing (resp. increasing) along the normalized Ricci flow. We also prove that any hyperbolic metric on a surface admits a neighborhood in the space of conformal negatively curved metrics in which the linear drift is greater or equal to the Liouville entropy, with equality if and only if the metric is hyperbolic.
item.dc:creator: Karen Butt, Alena Erchenko, Tristan Humbert

item.title: The inverse Monge--Amp\`ere flow on klt Fano varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.36414v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the long time existence of the inverse Monge--Amp\`ere flow on a klt $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano variety $X$. We further prove that $X$ admits a K\"ahler--Einstein metric if and only if the flow converges in $L^1$.
item.dc:creator: Jianchun Chu, Tam\'as Darvas, Yaxiong Liu

item.title: Klt varieties with semipositive anticanonical bundle : symmetric tensors, holonomy and structure
item.description: arXiv:2610.37002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The aim of this article is to study klt projective varieties such that the anticanonical bundle is semipositive from the differential-geometric point of view. The study of the holonomy of such varieties yields generalizations of several results. We show that the dimension of the space of symmetric differentials is bounded by a constant depending on the augmented irregularity, generalizing a result of Kobayashi. If we endow such a variety $X$ with a metric $\omega$ whose Ricci curvature is non-negative, then we show that the holonomy of the regular locus is compact. If we assume that $X$ has canonical singularities, then we show that the general fiber of the Albanese map can be decomposed into a product of irreducible Calabi-Yau varieties, irreducible holomorphic symplectic varieties and hereditarily rationally connected varieties by the holonomy generalizing a structure theorem of Campana, Demailly and Peternell. To conclude, we show that the fundamental group of the regular locus of such varieties is virtually abelian.
item.dc:creator: Louis Dailly

item.title: Measure of Maximal Entropy for Geodesic Flows on Noncompact Manifolds of Nonpositive Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.37439v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the variational characterization of the measure of maximal entropy on noncompact manifolds of nonpositive sectional curvature. Assuming that the deck transformation group contains an axial isometry with a rank-one axis and has a finite critical exponent, we prove that the supremum of the entropies of invariant probabilities equals the critical exponent and is attained if and only if the Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan (BMS) measure is finite. In that case, the measure of maximal entropy is unique and equals the normalized BMS measure. The proof combines conditional-entropy rigidity on the regular set with an HTS-based entropy exclusion on the singular set, overcoming both non-compactness and the loss of uniform hyperbolicity due to zero curvature. We also obtain mixing under a non-arithmetic length-spectrum assumption. For nonpositively curved surfaces of genus at least two, the existence of a closed Jacobi rank-one geodesic and the non-arithmeticity of the axial length spectrum are automatic.
item.dc:creator: Fei Liu, Xiaokai Liu

item.title: Bubble Tree Convergence for Minimisers of a Regularised Baby-Skyrme Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.37457v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study degree $1$ minimisers $u: (\Sigma,g) \to S^2$ for a Baby-Skyrme model with a Sacks-Uhlenbeck regularisation term $E^{\alpha}(u) = \frac{1}{2} \int_{\Sigma} (1+\vert \nabla u \vert^2)^{\alpha+1} -1 dv_g$ and establish convergence of degree $1$ minimisers to a simple bubble tree as $\alpha \to 0$. We also obtain a new no-neck result for the classical Sacks-Uhlenbeck energy $E^{\alpha}$.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Woodward

item.title: No Connectedness Lemma for Alexandrov spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.37476v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Since its introduction in 2003, Wilking's Connectedness Lemma has become a powerful tool in the study of manifolds with positive sectional curvature. In recent work of the authors, this has been extended to orbifolds. The purpose of this note is to exhibit counterexamples in the class of Alexandrov spaces for the Connectedness Lemma in both its ordinary and dual formulation. This answers a 2007 question of Wilking.
item.dc:creator: Jan Nienhaus, Dennis Wulle

item.title: Fisher Completions and Statistical Regularization of Wrapped Gaussian Families
item.description: arXiv:2610.37526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the intrinsic Fisher completion of the full-covariance wrapped Gaussian family on a fixed torus and relate its geometry to uniform estimation. The completion is homeomorphic to the total-variation closure. Every added law is, in suitable integer torus coordinates, a product of a uniform law and a lower-dimensional wrapped Gaussian. All these densities are positive and real analytic, but in dimension at least two no added point has a compact neighborhood. Small balls remain contractible, and explicit minimizing geodesics pass through added points. In dimension at least two, every fixed Fisher neighborhood of an added point has a positive minimax risk at every sample size. For subfamilies with a common positive lower bound on the variance in every nonzero integer direction, we prove that compactness of the completed closure is equivalent to uniform consistency in either $L^1$ or completed-Fisher loss. Equivalently, the Fourier moments must decay uniformly over the subfamily. A fixed covariance floor guarantees this condition without an upper covariance bound and gives $L^1$ risk at most $C_{\varepsilon,d}n^{-1/2}\{\log(n+1)\}^{d/4}$. A common-phase example illustrates how partially uniform limits can retain relative-phase information while remaining uniformly estimable.
item.dc:creator: Gunhee Cho, Hyun Chul Jang

item.title: Boundary Plateau Laws I
item.description: arXiv:2610.37559v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a complete list of the possible local shapes of soap films where they wet the whole wire. In rigorous terms, given a straight line $\ell \subset \mathbb R^3$, we study $2$-dimensional cones in $\mathbb R^3$ which contain $\ell$ and are Almgren minimizing with respect to $\ell$.
item.dc:creator: Camillo De Lellis, Federico Glaudo

item.title: Boundary Plateau Laws II
item.description: arXiv:2610.37560v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a straight line $\ell \subset \mathbb R^3$, we classify $2$-dimensional cones in $\mathbb R^3$ which contain $\ell$ and are Almgren minimizing with respect to $\ell$. The main idea of this paper is due to an LLM, and the paper was written by an LLM, under the guidance of the authors.
item.dc:creator: Camillo De Lellis, Federico Glaudo

item.title: A Li-Yau gradient estimate for the Finslerian logarithmic Schr\"{o}dinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2507.06237v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a local Li--Yau type gradient estimate for a nonlinear parabolic equation with logarithmic reaction on a forward complete Finsler metric measure manifold. The coefficients may depend on both space and time. The estimate uses a weighted Ricci curvature lower bound and explicit cutoff bounds for the divergence-form linearized Laplacian. We explain the role of this localization assumption when the reference direction varies with the solution. Applications include a local Harnack inequality for the equation with a potential and an upper bound for positive stationary solutions under a suitable cutoff exhaustion. An appendix gives a variational existence proof for positive bounded initial data, with quantitative bounds on every finite time interval, which is new as far as the authors know.
item.dc:creator: Duoxin Li, Zisu Zhao

item.title: Submanifolds with boundary in sub-Riemannian Heisenberg Groups
item.description: arXiv:2508.15634v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discuss the notion of submanifolds with boundary with intrinsic $C^1$ regularity in sub-Riemannian Heisenberg groups and we provide some examples. Eventually, we present a Stokes' Theorem for such submanifolds involving the integration of Rumin's differential forms in Heisenberg groups.
item.dc:creator: Marco Di Marco, Davide Vittone

item.title: Total curvature of convex hypersurfaces in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2601.13280v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that if the curvature of a Cartan-Hadamard $n$-manifold is constant near a convex hypersurface $\Gamma$, then the total Gauss-Kronecker curvature $\mathcal{G}(\Gamma)$ is not less than that of any convex hypersurface nested inside $\Gamma$. This extends Borb\'{e}ly's monotonicity theorem in hyperbolic space. It follows that $\mathcal{G}(\Gamma)$ is bounded below by the volume of the unit sphere in Euclidean space $\mathbf{R}^n$. If $n=3$ or $\Gamma$ is $\mathcal{C}^{1,1}$, it suffices that the curvature be constant on $\Gamma$.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Ghomi, John Ioannis Stavroulakis

item.title: Quantitative stability and strict inequalities for the Escobar functional
item.description: arXiv:2601.22665v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For Euclidean domains whose boundaries are sufficiently close to a sphere in $C^2$, we bound the deficit of the Escobar constant from below by the squared $H^{3/2}$ norm of the boundary graph, after fixing its constant and first spherical harmonics. This holds in every dimension $n\ge3$ and implies a bound in Fraenkel asymmetry with optimal quadratic power. Under fixed $C^{6,\alpha}$ and size bounds, the asymmetry estimate also holds for star-shaped domains in dimensions $n\ge6$. For compact Riemannian manifolds with minimal boundary and uniform geometric bounds, we prove $S_\ast-C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)\ge ca^4/\log(\Lambda/a)$ in dimension six and $S_\ast-C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)\ge ca^4$ in higher dimensions, where $a=\|\mathring{\mathrm{II}}\|_{L^\infty}>0$. A family satisfying the same bounds has deficit comparable to $a^{8/3}$, excluding uniform lower bounds with smaller powers. We also compute the cubic coefficient of the standard boundary bubble quotient and give uniform remainder estimates.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee, Utsab Sarkar

item.title: On $q$-convex hypersurfaces in Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2604.20695v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that any closed, convex hypersurface in an $(n+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with $\lceil \frac{n}{2} \rceil$-positive curvature operator is a rational homology sphere with finite fundamental group. The same conclusion holds for any $\lceil \frac{n}{2} \rceil$-convex hypersurface, provided that the mean curvature satisfies a sharp pinching condition. Both results follow from more general vanishing and estimation theorems for the Betti numbers of closed $q$-convex immersed hypersurfaces in $(n+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds, under a lower bound on the average of the smallest $(n-p)$ eigenvalues of the curvature operator.
item.dc:creator: Giulio Colombo, Christos-Raent Onti

item.title: Minimal submanifolds confined in space
item.description: arXiv:2605.15031v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Already in $\mathbb{R}^4$, there are many minimal hypersurfaces but few structural results. The half-space theorem fails there: higher-dimensional catenoids are among the many examples contained in a slab. Nevertheless, we show that in any dimension and codimension, the height of a minimal submanifold controls its volume growth: confinement to a narrow cone forces polynomial growth, and sublinear height forces Euclidean growth, the slowest possible. Thus volume bounds, which regularity theory assumes, follow from height alone. The key is a volume doubling theorem that converts geometric confinement into quantitative rigidity: if an $n$-dimensional stationary integral varifold lies in a thin slab at a given scale, then its volume doubling ratio at that scale is bounded by a universal constant. Iterating this gives the polynomial growth bounds above. Sublinear height is exactly the borderline for Euclidean growth: examples grow at least like $r^{n+4\epsilon^2/5}$ in cones of aperture $\epsilon$. From Euclidean volume growth, we obtain an optimal Bernstein theorem, in all dimensions, for stable minimal hypersurfaces with sublinear height growth, generalizing results of Moser, Bombieri--De Giorgi--Miranda, Trudinger, Caffarelli--Nirenberg--Spruck, and Ecker--Huisken.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Holck Colding, William P. Minicozzi II

item.title: A dichotomy for minimal submanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2607.29502v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We survey a circle of recent results showing that a minimal submanifold obeys a dichotomy: either it fills up space, spreading out like a space-filling curve, or it is confined, and confinement forces quantitative restrictions. On the confined side these restrictions are both geometric and function-theoretic: Euclidean volume growth, an optimal rate of convergence of the density, complex-curve rigidity for stable surfaces in $\bf{R}^4$, and a Liouville theorem forcing slowly growing harmonic functions on minimal disks to be constant. A prototypical restriction is Euclidean volume growth, which in these results is forced by the geometry rather than assumed. The mechanism is a volume doubling theorem that converts geometric confinement into quantitative rigidity: a stationary integral varifold trapped in a thin slab at a given scale cannot double its volume by more than a universal factor. We explain how this principle, and the height-excess bounds behind it, produce Euclidean volume growth for submanifolds of sublinearly growing height in every dimension and codimension, the optimal density rate in a slab, the complex-curve and Liouville rigidity above, a higher-codimension Bernstein theorem for disks, one-sided volume bounds, and an optimal stable Bernstein theorem in all dimensions generalizing Moser, Bombieri-De Giorgi-Miranda, Caffarelli-Nirenberg-Spruck and Ecker-Huisken. We describe three regimes with sharp borderlines. In narrow cones the volume grows polynomially with exponent $n+O(\varepsilon^2)$, and the order $\varepsilon^2$ is attained; in wide cones the growth can be arbitrarily fast. For holomorphic curves in $\mathbb{C}^2$, there are also three regimes and the borderline is determined by the K\"ahler angle.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Holck Colding, William P. Minicozzi II

item.title: On bubbling of Fueter maps
item.description: arXiv:2608.26803v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study bubbling for sequences of solutions of the Hamiltonian-perturbed Fueter equation. By Walpuski's compactness theorem, a bounded-energy sequence converges weakly to a Fueter map, with energy loss recorded by a defect measure supported on a codimension 2 rectifiable set. Assuming that the limiting map has no non-removable singularities and the bubbles attach to it on a subset of the bubbling locus of positive measure, we show that the limiting Hamiltonian lies in an exceptional subset of infinite codimension. The proof combines quantitative control of rational sweepout loci in hyperk\"ahler manifolds with a transversality argument. We expect the attachment assumption to be automatic and follow from a suitable no-neck result. This strongly suggests that, in the absence of non-removable singularities, bubbling of Hamiltonian-perturbed Fueter maps is highly nongeneric.
item.dc:creator: Jacek Rzemieniecki

item.title: Blaschke Conjecture and Complex Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2609.23822v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a complex-geometric approach to the Blaschke conjecture, i.e., that a manifold whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is isometric to a compact rank-one symmetric space (CROSS). In particular, we introduce the great quadric fibration, a complex analogue of the great sphere fibration. Requiring its total space to be a complex submanifold simultaneously explains many properties that a Blaschke manifold is expected to possess, including its Clifford structure, Hopf fibration, and diffeomorphism class. Furthermore, the great quadric bundle coincides with the variety of minimal rational tangents (VMRT) of the ambient Fano variety in the standard CROSS cases, and we explain this through a bend-and-break argument in the setting of the Blaschke conjecture under a suitable complexification assumption. Combining this with Hwang-Mok VMRT recognition, we prove the Blaschke conjecture for manifolds admitting an adapted complex structure on their entire tangent bundles.
item.dc:creator: Kyobeom Song

item.title: Topology, Morse Index, and Area of Minimal Surfaces in Three-Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2609.32001v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that, in every closed Riemannian three-manifold $(M^3,\bar g)$, there exists a constant $C=C(M,\bar g)>0$ such that every closed smoothly embedded minimal surface $\Sigma\subset M$ satisfies $b_1(\Sigma;\mathbb{Z}_2)\le C\bigl(\operatorname{Ind}(\Sigma)+\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma)\bigr)$, establishing Song's additive genus-index-area conjecture. For closed connected orientable two-sided minimal immersions, we prove the universal inequality $\gamma(\Sigma)\le8\operatorname{Ind}(\Sigma)$ in positive Ricci curvature and the estimate $\gamma(\Sigma)\le C(M,\bar g)\operatorname{Ind}(\Sigma)$ in positive scalar curvature. In the latter case, we also bound both area and total curvature by $C(M,\bar g)(1+\operatorname{Ind}(\Sigma))$.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Caniato

item.title: Examples of topological sphere $\lambda$-self-expander
item.description: arXiv:2610.10634v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A $\lambda$-self-expander $F: M^n\to \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is the solution of the isoperimetric problem of weight $e^{\frac{|x|^2}{4}}$. In this paper, for sufficiently large $\lambda$, we construct an immersed non-embedded spherical $\lambda$-self-expander in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ with the mean curvature $H>0$. Moreover, we obtain the explicit solution for $n=2$.
item.dc:creator: Mengdan Qi

item.title: CMC foliations on Euclidean spaces are minimal foliations
item.description: arXiv:2610.20406v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we provide a complete answer to one of the most classical conjectures in differential geometry (of foliations). More precisely, we present a complete positive answer to the classical conjecture, due to Meeks III, P\'erez, and Ros (2008), that states that every foliation on $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ by (possibly varying) CMC hypersurfaces is a foliation by minimal hypersurfaces. Moreover, if $n\leq 6$, such a CMC foliation must consist of parallel hyperplanes.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Edson Sampaio, Euripedes Carvalho da Silva

item.title: Complete steady and shrinking gradient Yamabe solitons
item.description: arXiv:2610.21078v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we show that complete steady gradient Yamabe solitons are either rotationally symmetric manifolds or scalar-flat manifolds. We also classify nontrivial complete shrinking gradient Yamabe solitons.
item.dc:creator: Shun Maeta

item.title: Characterizations of the plane and the catenoid as capillary minimal surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.32447v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove that an annular capillary minimal surface outside the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with one complete embedded end and finite total curvature must be either part of the plane or part of the catenoid. The proofs are based on the use of the Weierstrass data through the Hopf differential and associated holomorphic functions. For a planar end, we control the second fundamental form, while for a catenoidal end, we analyze the Gauss map in more detail using the boundary condition. We also prove nonexistence results for annular free boundary minimal surfaces with one end asymptotic to the end of Enneper's surface, under appropriate conditions. Finally, we establish an exterior analogue of Choe's result on capillary minimal surfaces with vertices.
item.dc:creator: Eungbeom Yeon

item.title: Genus Increase in Closed Mean Curvature Flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.35000v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct closed mean curvature flows with arbitrarily large genus increase in every smooth Riemannian three-manifold, giving counterexamples to Ilmanen's genus-reduction conjecture. We prove that a compact hypersurface with a single isolated conical singularity and a power rate of convergence to its cone admits a mean curvature flow whose forward rescaled limit is a prescribed expander in the tangent space at the singular point, smoothly asymptotic to that cone. Combining this theorem with closed mean curvature flows with prescribed tangent flows (arXiv:2405.15577, arXiv:2607.23879) and the noncompact counterexample (arXiv:2605.09657) gives the desired examples.
item.dc:creator: Jingwen Chen

item.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35492v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $V_{g,n}$ denote the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of genus-$g$ hyperbolic surfaces with $n$ cusps. Mirzakhani and Zograf obtained a complete asymptotic expansion as $g\to\infty$ for fixed $n$; its terms are effectively powers of $n^2/g$, so it degenerates once $n$ is of order $\sqrt g$. We prove an asymptotic expansion in inverse powers of the genus that is uniform in all $n\ge0$. The leading term is an explicit saddle-point expression whose saddle moves with the cusp density $n/g$. It has relative error $O(g^{-1})$, and truncation at an order proportional to $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\exp(-a\sqrt g))$ for some $a>0$. For fixed $n$, the leading term confirms Zograf's conjecture that the constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics is $1/\sqrt\pi$. We also determine the asymptotic profiles of volume ratios, uniformly in the number of cusps, and of adjacent coefficients of the one-boundary volume polynomial, uniformly in the degree; this answers two questions of Mirzakhani. The proof uses a positive recursion for mixed $\kappa_1$--$\psi$ intersection numbers, normalized at the pure-$\psi$ endpoint, and a local limit theorem in the number of cusps.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyi Li, Qihang Wang

item.title: Silent Orbits and Cancellations in the Wave Trace
item.description: arXiv:2408.09238v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper shows that the wave trace of a bounded and strictly convex planar domain may be arbitrarily smooth in a neighborhood of some point in the length spectrum. In other words, the Poisson relation, which asserts that the singular support of the wave trace is contained in the closure of $\pm$ the length spectrum, can almost be made into a strict inclusion. To do so, we construct large families of domains for which there exist multiple periodic billiard orbits having the same length but different Maslov indices. Using the microlocal Balian-Bloch-Zelditch parametrix for wave invariants developed in our previous paper, we solve a large system of equations for the boundary curvature jets, which leads to the required cancellations. We call such periodic orbits silent, since they are undetectable from the ostensibly audible wave trace. Such cancellations show that there are potential limitations in using the wave trace for inverse spectral problems and, more fundamentally, that the Laplace spectrum and the length spectrum are inherently different mathematical objects, at least insofar as the wave trace is concerned.
item.dc:creator: Illya Koval, Amir Vig

item.title: A geometric--analytic proof of the reverse isoperimetric inequality in Einstein gravity
item.description: arXiv:2508.13235v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a geometric--analytic proof of the reverse isoperimetric inequality for compact AdS black hole horizons in Einstein gravity. At fixed thermodynamic volume, a York slice/Jacobi variation of the gravitational action shows that the spherical Schwarzschild--AdS solution is a strict local entropy maximum against generic non-spherical deformations. The finite global extension is formulated within the hypotheses of the Sherif--Dunsby (SD) rigidity theorem: compactness and spherical topology, the required intrinsic Ricci decomposition $\mathrm{Ric}_h=\alpha\,\mathbf e\!\otimes\!\mathbf e+\beta N$ with $\alpha\neq\beta$, a proper conformal transformation of the hypersurface metric given by $\widetilde h_{ab}=e^{2\varphi}h_{ab}$ that preserves its intrinsic scalar curvature, $\widetilde R\equiv R[\widetilde h]=R[h]\equiv R>0$, and negative sheet expansion. Compactness and $S^3$ topology are built into the class considered here. In the static spherical sector such as Schwarzschild--AdS and RN--AdS, the SD Ricci form is naturally realized while it is an additional restriction for Kerr--AdS case. For the $S^3$ topology, a positive Yamabe type conformal class exists for which the Yamabe theorem provides a representative of positive and constant scalar-curvature. We further restrict to the scalar-curvature preserving conformal transformation required by the SD theorem. The negative sheet expansion is obtained using gravitational focusing. Within this admissible class, a non-round Kerr--AdS horizon cannot maximize the entropy, while fixed thermodynamic volume selects the corresponding round Schwarzschild--AdS comparator. The analysis thus establishes a generic local entropy maximum and a finite global result within the stated geometric rigidity class, identifying the role of gravity in reversing the ordinary isoperimetric problem.
item.dc:creator: Naman Kumar

item.title: On the distribution kernels of Toeplitz operators on CR manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2512.16506v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the distribution kernel of a Toeplitz operator associated with a classical pseudodifferential operator on a compact, embeddable, strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold. The main result consists of a formula for the values at the diagonal of the second coefficient in the expansion of the symbol of the kernel. We also establish asymptotic expansions for Toeplitz operators on the positive part of a compact not necessary strictly pseudoconvex CR orbifold under certain natural assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Chin-Yu Hsiao, Ood Shabtai

item.title: Unimodular random ideal hyperbolic polyhedra: geometric characteristics and random walks
item.description: arXiv:2601.14909v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We initiate a systematic study of unimodular random infinite ideal hyperbolic polyhedra in three-dimensional hyperbolic space, developing a geometric and probabilistic theory of their global behavior. At the heart of this theory is an intrinsic geometric characteristic, determined entirely by the dihedral angles surrounding a polyhedral face. We establish a unimodular Gauss-Bonnet identity and show that the expectation of this local geometric invariant completely determines the global conformal type: under suitable assumptions, a random ideal polyhedron is almost surely parabolic precisely when the expected characteristic vanishes, and hyperbolic precisely when it is negative. This provides a sharp geometric classification of random infinite ideal polyhedra. Building on the correspondence with ideal circle patterns, we further develop a refined Ring Lemma that yields quantitative geometric control without bounded-degree assumptions. Combining these geometric tools with unimodular probability methods, we identify the Poisson boundary of the face random walk and establish positive linear hyperbolic speed. Together, these results establish a local-to-global framework linking intrinsic dihedral geometry, conformal uniformization, and stochastic behavior at infinity for unimodular random infinite ideal hyperbolic polyhedra.
item.dc:creator: Huabin Ge, Yangxiang Lu, Chuwen Wang, Tian Zhou

item.title: A Sharp Regularity Threshold for Uniqueness in Riemannian Calder\'on-type Problems
item.description: arXiv:2605.21705v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a sharp regularity threshold for uniqueness in two anisotropic Calder\'on-type inverse problems in dimension $n\ge 3$. The main setting is the Riemannian Schr\"odinger problem with fixed scalar potential: for a prescribed nonconstant analytic function $V$, we study whether the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of $-\Delta_g+V$ on a domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ determines the unknown metric $g$. The natural gauge is the group of boundary-fixing diffeomorphisms preserving $V$. We show that, while analytic metrics are uniquely determined modulo this gauge by a minor adaptation of the Lassas--Uhlmann reconstruction theorem, uniqueness fails densely in every non-analytic Gevrey class $G^\sigma$, $\sigma>1$. In fact, our counterexamples are not isometric in the sense that they are not connected by the pushforward of any diffeomorphism of $\overline\Omega$. We also prove the analogous sharp threshold for the anisotropic Calder\'on problem at fixed nonzero frequency, thereby upgrading the previously known finite-regularity counterexamples to Gevrey and $C^\infty$ regularity. The two constructions use different scalar mechanisms: for fixed potentials, the nonconstant potential itself provides a local coordinate, while at nonzero frequency one uses a compactly supported prescribed-Jacobian lemma in Gevrey spaces. Thus analyticity is the exact threshold for uniqueness in both problems.
item.dc:creator: Thierry Daud\'e, Alberto Enciso, Bernard Helffer, Niky Kamran, Fran\c{c}ois Nicoleau

item.title: Continuum-wise hyperbolicity is exactly the pseudo-Anosov dynamics with spine singularities
item.description: arXiv:2606.11943v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a complete structural classification for cw$_F$-hyperbolic surface homeomorphisms. Specifically, we prove that a surface homeomorphism is cw$_F$-hyperbolic if, and only if, it is a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism whose singularities consist exclusively of spines (1-prongs). Furthermore, we classify these systems up to topological conjugacy, showing that every such homeomorphism is conjugate to either an Anosov automorphism on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ or to a standard hyperelliptic quotient on $\mathbb{S}^2$ of a hyperbolic affine toral map. As a rigid consequence of this classification, we show that such dynamics are strictly obstructed on surfaces of genus greater than one, the Klein bottle, and the projective plane.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Arruda, Bernardo Carvalho, Piotr Oprocha, Alberto Sarmiento

item.title: Statistics on Yau's conjecture: Variance asymptotics
item.description: arXiv:2607.09946v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the probabilistic counterpart of Yau's conjecture on the nodal volume of Laplace eigenfunctions on compact manifolds, by studying the high-frequency variance asymptotics of Riemannian random waves. Theorem A gives quantitative bounds on the fluctuations of their nodal volume for all regimes of spectral windows, including the monochromatic one, of spectral size 1. For every non-monochromatic window the variance has the exact order $1/N$, where $N$ is the dimension of the underlying space of eigenfunctions, on any compact manifold. In the monochromatic regime, on manifolds without conjugate points and in particular on negatively curved ones, we prove that the variance is $o(1/N)$: this improves the previous best bound, cf. Canzani and Hanin 2020, to its square divided by a logarithmic factor, and exhibits a form of Berry's cancellation, relative to the natural scale $1/N$, for monochromatic random waves on such chaotic manifolds. Our proofs rely on a local and global analysis combining the Kac-Rice formula, the Wiener--It\^o chaos decomposition recently obtained by the authors Stecconi and Todino 2025, and a sharp analysis of the error in the pointwise Weyl law associated to an arbitrary spectral window (Theorem B). We also introduce a general machinery (Theorem C) that yields variance decay for the nodal volume of an arbitrary Gaussian field under broad geometric conditions, subject to correlation decay assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Michele Stecconi, Anna Paola Todino

item.title: K\"ahler landscapes for complex neural network descents and guarantees including a search and destroy of the Calabi-Yau manifold
item.description: arXiv:2608.19584v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study landscapes for complex-parameterized networks. Our approach is motivated with an information-theoretic manifold perspective of the parameter and via classical optimization guarantees although of complex geometric variety such as through Dolbeault asymptotics. The descent path admits a K\"ahler information metric under a cross-entropy via the Wirtinger Hessian on the log-likelihood potential. We restrict attention to a descent update rule with natural gradient descent via a differentiated loss scaled by the inverse metric, so the descent path remains in the holomorphic tangent bundle. We emphasize Calabi-Yau information manifolds which profane theoretical guarantees via an ill-curvature-conditioned, or lack thereof, landscape. We focus on Calabi-Yau metrics specifically in a non-compact setting with a global potential, so defined geometrically rather than invoking the topological requirements of the Calabi conjecture. In non-compact settings, we can write the metric determinant with respect to a background in terms of a function, pluriharmonic or real. Using Yau's Liouville theorem, we get a partial eigenvalue blow-up effect. In an empirical setting, a Ricci-flat metric will not form, but a blow-up can be a local condition and can hold empirically on open sets even partially in generalized K\"ahler cases due to lower bounds on the Ricci potential. Moreover, it has been discovered that negative curvature subverts the loss landscape, specifically sectional curvature, so we expand on this and draw interconnections to negative-definite Ricci curvature. Our arguments primarily exist via geometric modality, although we establish roots in deep learning theory such as through asymptotics at initialization and connections through failure modes of neural network guarantees under vanishing and negative Ricci curvature.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Gracyk

item.title: Reconstruction of Heat Geometry from a Scalar Process
item.description: arXiv:2609.27967v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A smooth scalar process with one fixed Gaussian covariance kernel determines any finite graded family of symmetric Hilbert tensors up to a common orthogonal isomorphism of their minimal supports. For two heat tensors, its law determines a closed positive-dimensional Riemannian manifold, a Euclidean bundle, its connection and potential, and the unknown heat time, up to isometry and gauge. The quadratic tensor recovers the scaled generator; the quartic tensor recovers the spatial norm and volume, which fix the time scale. For compact finite-dimensional RCD spaces, the same law determines the measured space with distance divided by the square root of the heat time.
item.dc:creator: Obayda Julien Assaad
